title: Interacting with ontology-based databases using machine learning
related_application_signals: claims benefit of US provisional application 63/559,708 filed 2024-02-29

source_provenance.note: Ephemeral request-token parameters are intentionally not persisted.

classification_signals: G06F16/3344 natural-language analysis for query execution
G06F16/24522 translation of natural-language queries to structured queries
publicly_described_functional_concepts: natural-language requests translated into one or more database queries for ontology-backed data
use of graph and relational databases behind one ontology abstraction
prompting or training an LLM with examples that map user requests to structured queries
selection among candidate queries using efficiency-oriented criteria
generation of ontology API function calls from natural-language requests
coordinated updates to ontology data and ontology-level metadata
preservation of ontology objects, links, properties, versions, provenance, and access controls outside the LLM itself

scope_model.analysis_loop: receive authorized natural-language request -> resolve ontology context -> classify read versus mutation intent -> generate candidate graph/relational/API operations -> validate syntax/schema/policy -> rank or select candidate -> execute through least-privilege adapter -> normalize result -> preserve provenance/audit -> return result
building_patterns_relevant_to_independen: keep ontology data in authoritative graph/relational stores rather than relying on LLM memory
treat the LLM as a planner/compiler that emits constrained intermediate operations
separate read-only query generation from ontology mutation paths
require schema-aware validation before executing generated queries or function calls
bind generated operations to least-privilege credentials and object-level authorization
support multiple query backends through independently designed adapters
retain candidate query provenance, model version, schema version, and execution result
prefer dry-run or explain modes before write operations
use deterministic query linting and policy checks around probabilistic generation
require explicit human approval for high-impact ontology mutations

independent_claim_themes: natural-language requests converted by an LLM into graph/database queries for ontology-backed data
ontology data represented through typed objects and links with data distributed across database systems
training or prompting patterns for generating ontology API function calls
candidate-query selection and execution for ontology access or update workflows
claim_scope_signals.legal_scope_rule: Patent scope depends on controlling claims, prosecution history, legal status, and jurisdiction. This record is an engineering research abstraction only.

family_signals.territorial_status_rule: Do not infer worldwide rights or freedom to operate from this US publication; recheck each national or regional register before legal or commercial decisions.

use_for: natural-language exploration of authorized ontology data

design_divergence_defaults: use independently designed query-planning prompts and intermediate representations
insert deterministic schema/policy validation between model generation and execution
separate mutation planning from mutation execution with an explicit approval boundary
rank candidate operations using independently selected safety, cost, latency, and complexity criteria
keep model context retrieval separate from authoritative ontology storage
maintain a complete audit record of generated operations, selected operations, and execution outcomes

mandatory_safety_boundaries: authorized ontology and database access only
separation of read and write execution paths
